title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
Problem VI of E443 concerns a uniform elastic lamina (Euler–Bernoulli beam) with both ends A and B free and a pin ('stylus') at an interior point C, at distances α from A and β from B, with α+β=a. Euler seeks its normal modes.

In modern terms each segment satisfies y'''' = (θ/b)^4 y, with time factor cos(θθt). The general solution is a combination of cos, sin, cosh and sinh, which Euler writes as A cos Φ + B sin Φ + C e^Φ + D e^{-Φ}, with Φ = θx/b. Each segment uses its own abscissa: x is measured from A toward C, and x' from B toward C.

Free-end conditions (zero moment y''=0 and zero shear y'''=0 at x=0) give:
- −A+C+D=0
- −B+C−D=0

Pin condition: with ζ=θα/b, the pin y(α)=0 gives A cos ζ + B sin ζ + C e^ζ + D e^{−ζ} = 0.

Euler then lists y', y'' and y''' at C so that the interface conditions can be imposed. He does the same for the other segment, with ζ'=θβ/b. That gives six equations for eight unknowns.

On the next page the remaining two conditions are slope continuity and curvature (moment) continuity at C. Eliminating the coefficients yields one transcendental frequency equation in ζ, with ζ:ζ'=α:β fixed. The jump in the third derivatives gives the reaction force of the pin, which Euler sets aside.

The page serves to set up an interior-support (two-span, interface-matching) eigenvalue problem for a free–free beam.
errors: Typographical: in the formula for (dy'/dx') the second term is printed 'B cos ζ'' instead of B' cos ζ'.
Typographical: the second-derivative label for the second segment is printed (ddy/dx'^2) instead of (ddy'/dx'^2).
Typographical: in (d^3y/dx^3) for the first segment the last exponential is printed as 'e^{-'}' rather than e^{-ζ}.

No substantive error on this page. The derivative formulas and the free-end conditions check out. The next page's interface conditions (dy/dx = dy'/dx' and y''+y''=0) are correct only if y' is counted on the opposite side of the axis. This amounts to a point-reflection of the second segment through C, which the equal-angle remark ACE=BCF on the previous page supports. With y' counted the same way as y, the conditions would instead read y_x = −y'_{x'} and y''=y''. The convention is consistent but left implicit.

ideas.what: Free-end boundary conditions y''=y'''=0 applied to the cos/sin/exp general solution of the beam equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli (1730s–1740s), refined in E443
ideas.where_published: Euler's Additamentum to the Methodus inveniendi (1744) and earlier vibration papers; E443 itself

ideas.what: Splitting the beam at an interior pin into two segments with separate local coordinates and matching conditions (zero deflection, continuous slope and moment, shear jump equal to the reaction)
ideas.modern_name: Interface/matching conditions for multi-span beams; precursor of transfer-matrix and continuous-beam eigenvalue analysis
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E443) for vibrating beams; for static continuous beams Clapeyron (1857) and Navier
ideas.where_published: E443 (this problem); discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II 11/2)

ideas.what: Remark that the pin produces a 'saltus in lege continuitatis' (jump in shear) whose size gives the force on the pin, from the third derivatives
ideas.modern_name: Shear discontinuity / support reaction at an interior support
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (here); standard in later beam theory

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine setup of an interior-pinned free–free beam eigenproblem. E443 and its new vibration species, including this interior-support problem, are analysed in Truesdell's 1960 history, so nothing here seems absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In (dy'/dx') read B' cos ζ' (the print itself shows 'B cos', a printer's error).
Third-derivative line for the first segment: the print shows 'D e^{-'}'; intended D e^{-ζ}.
